facts: LLM agents are becoming GPU kernel engineers, but they still tune kernels without seeing where the time goes.

Hardware profilers report how busy each unit was, not where each warp's time went; intra-kernel tracers can show it, but only with hand-placed probes and a recompilation that alters the very kernel being measured.
We present Warpline, which gives agents this view automatically while leaving the kernel essentially unchanged.
Warpline analyzes the binary to decide which events to record and inserts probes into the binary itself without recompilation or any manual step.
It then aligns the trace with hardware profiling data on one unified timeline.

Because it needs only the binary, it can regenerate this evidence for every new version of the kernel at whatever level the agent edits it (source, IR, or PTX), closing the optimization loop without human intervention.

On NVIDIA B200, across 35 kernels in Triton, CuTe DSL, and CUDA C++, Warpline adds a median overhead of 1.2% and leaves a median 99.9% of executed instructions unchanged, whereas existing tracers have median overheads of
Warpline also traces closed-source kernels, which these tracers cannot.
